_comment: Instance data for core/scripts/collab-watch.sh (skill collab-watch). Copy to
.claude/rules/collab-watch.json and replace every <placeholder> — the plan step refuses
a file that still carries one, instead of arming a watch whose API calls fail silently.
shared_memory   the local clone of the org's shared-memory repo (may start with ~). Drop
the block if there is none.
repo_watches    one entry per poll cadence. `tag` names the cursor and the lock — unique.
A repo appears in ONE entry only. List the repos where collaborators
actually talk: the core, the suites they own, the marketplace.
parallel_sessions  watch Claude sessions joining/leaving this brain's repo.
parties         who is who. id = the `von:`/sender value in the shared-memory repo,
github = the account that pushes, label = the name used in prose,
kind = self (the operator's own machines) | peer (a collaborator).
Two own machines share one account — that is why scopes select by
party and a login filter is never the default.
Intervals in seconds, minimum 30. Change cadence HERE, not in a script or a rule.
The AIs talk through PR comments and shared memory: a reply waits up to one interval on
each side, so 300 s meant up to ten minutes per question and answer. Shared memory is a
git fetch (no API budget): 30 s. The repos where the AIs talk (core) poll every 60 s; the
rest stays at 300 s, because every own machine polls under ONE account (5000 API calls an
hour). The repo watch slows itself when that budget runs low (WATCH_RATE_FLOOR_PCT).
